title: STRENGTHENING NARCO COORDINATION CENTRE
body_text:
Government has strengthened inter-ministerial and inter-agency coordination through restructured 4-tier (Apex, Executive, State & District level) Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism by inclusion of various stakeholders at all four levels. It provides a structured, institutionalized platform for coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments and enforcement  agencies  for  monitoring drug trafficking, precursor diversion,
demand reduction and rehabilitation, resulting in improved enforcement outcomes and intelligence-sharing. NCORD has been consistently active and functional at the Apex, Executive, State and District levels. So far, 10 Apex NCORD meetings and 7 Executive NCORD meetings have been held to guide policy formulation, enhance inter-ministerial coordination and review the overall narcotics control framework. At the operational level, 272 State NCORD meetings and 16,187 District NCORD meetings have been conducted across the country, enabling coordinated enforcement action, intelligence sharing and regular monitoring of drug trafficking trends at the grassroots level. These meetings have strengthened cooperation among agencies, facilitated joint operations and supported focused interventions against drug trafficking networks operating across States. The status of implementation of directions of NCORD Committee meetings are regularly reviewed for further necessary action. Inputs of these NCORD meetings have been proved useful in drafting the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). Further, an NCORD Portal has been created to act as a platform for all drug and NCB related information and also as a total Knowledge Management System (KMS) for all four tiers of the NCORD mechanism. It also acts as a repository of information on the anti-drug abuse initiatives of the Government of India. In
addition, initiatives like Madak-Padarth Nished Asoochna Kendra (MANAS) - 24x7 toll-free helpline (1933), National Integrated Database on Arrested Narco-Offenders (NIDAAN) portal, Mission SPANDAN– Partnership with spiritual institutions for awareness have emerged out of NCORD mechanism.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the 4-tier Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism—Apex, Executive, State and District levels—has been restructured and strengthened to improve inter-ministerial and inter-agency coordination against drug trafficking. So far, 10 Apex, 7 Executive, 272 State and 16,187 District NCORD meetings have been held, feeding into a Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) by the Narcotics Control Bureau. Related initiatives include the NCORD Portal (a knowledge management system), the MANAS 24x7 helpline (1933), the NIDAAN database of arrested narco-offenders, and Mission SPANDAN involving spiritual institutions in anti-drug awareness.
enrichment.context:
NCORD was constituted in 2016 and later restructured in 2019 into a multi-tier structure to overcome fragmented enforcement by multiple agencies (Narcotics Control Bureau, Central Bureau of Narcotics, state police, customs, Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, etc.) tackling drug trafficking, precursor chemical diversion, and demand reduction. India's location between the 'Golden Crescent' (Afghanistan-Pakistan-Iran) and 'Golden Triangle' (Myanmar-Laos-Thailand) drug production zones makes coordinated narcotics control a persistent internal security and public health challenge, especially given rising synthetic drug trafficking via maritime and postal routes.

This coordination architecture ties into India's broader anti-narcotics strategy under the NCB, which also runs public awareness and de-addiction campaigns. Programmes like the MANAS helpline and NIDAAN database reflect a shift toward technology-enabled, data-driven drug control, while Mission SPANDAN's partnership with spiritual institutions signals an attempt to leverage social and religious networks for demand reduction, a softer complement to the traditionally supply-side, enforcement-heavy approach (seizures, arrests, precursor tracking) under the NDPS Act, 1985.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism in India:
1. It is a four-tier structure comprising Apex, Executive, State and District levels.
2. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) is not involved in NCORD activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: NCORD is a four-tier mechanism (Apex, Executive, State, District) coordinated under the Ministry of Home Affairs, with the NCB actively involved, including drafting the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029). Hence statements 1 and 2 are correct, while statement 3 is false.

prelims_questions.question: The 24x7 toll-free helpline '1933' associated with anti-drug initiatives in India is known as:
prelims_questions.explanation: MANAS (Madak-Padarth Nished Asoochna Kendra) is the 24x7 toll-free helpline (number 1933) that emerged from the NCORD mechanism for reporting drug-related information.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the restructured NCORD (Narco-Coordination) mechanism in strengthening India's drug trafficking control framework. What challenges persist in inter-agency and Centre-State coordination on narcotics enforcement?

India's approach to drug demand reduction has increasingly combined technology-driven surveillance with community and institutional partnerships. Critically examine this shift with reference to initiatives like NIDAAN, MANAS and Mission SPANDAN.
